race_name: Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps

top_categories.workout_context: 136ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
14,000ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 103, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
14,000ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps. Train it until it feels boring.

Road-specific control matters at Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps. Practice on paved Sierra Nevada mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 103 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 103 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 14,000ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 14,000ft of climbing on paved Sierra Nevada mountain passes does to your power file on race day.
103 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps’s 103 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Death Ride — Tour of the California Alps includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. High-altitude sun exposure — intense UV above 7,000 ft; Thin air above 8,000 ft affects performance.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, VO2max, and Over Under to prepare you for 103 miles of paved sierra nevada mountain passes in Markleeville, Alpine County, California.
